children: US crude oil inventories fell by 11.12 million barrels in the week ending October 9th, far exceeding expectations for a 1.9 million-barrel increase and marking the largest draw since late January.
In the previous week, crude stocks fell by 2.09 million barrels.
Meanwhile, Cushing inventories rose by 1.82 million barrels, following an increase of 866,000 barrels in the prior week.
Gasoline inventories increased by 1.1 million barrels in the week ending October 7th, while distillate stocks fell by 1.5 million barrels.
US crude oil production rose to 13.98 million barrels per day in the week ending October 2nd, up from 13.95 million bpd a week earlier.

title: US Crude Inventories Post Largest Draw Since January
